title: human-in-the-loop-rollout-lock-with-telemetry-reconcile
author: Aisha N. Patel
release_notes: Add human-in-the-loop rollout lock and telemetry reconciliation hook. Backwards-compatible API changes to rollout controller config schema. Requires console feature flag to enable.
description:
Summary: Implement a human-in-the-loop (HITL) rollout lock and telemetry reconciliation step for staged model promotes. Motivated by a recent incident where automatic promotes bypassed a flaky metric; this PR adds a lockable checkpoint between automated gating and traffic promotion so an operator can inspect telemetry snapshots, optionally run a dry-run smoke test, and then approve/abort.

What this changes: - Rollout controller: adds new 'hitl_lock' phase to the promote FSM with explicit states: LOCKED, PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, ABORTED. The controller persists lock state in the rollout ledger so restarts are safe. - Telemetry reconcile hook: a pluggable step that captures pre-promote and post-shadow metric snapshots (latency p50/p95, error-rate, perplexity delta for eval sets) and exposes a compact diff in Console UI. - Dry-run smoke runner: a lightweight replay of a small synthetic traffic sample against the candidate model in shadow mode that can be triggered before approval. - API/Config: rollout spec gains optional fields: hitl.enabled (bool), hitl.timeout (duration), hitl.required_reviewers (list), hitl.dry_run_traffic_fraction. Defaults are off. - Console: operator view for locked rollouts with telemetry diff, links to sample payloads, one-click approve/abort, and a link to open a Linear ticket pre-populated with the snapshot. - Docs and playbook: docs/rollouts/hitl.md with operator guidance and incident playbook for aborting/fast-reverting.

Checklist: - [x] Controller FSM & persistence - [x] Telemetry reconcile snapshot + diff - [x] Dry-run smoke runner integration - [x] Console UI components and approval flow - [x] API & rollback compatibility tests - [x] E2E test harness exercising locked state and approve/abort - [x] Docs & runbook - [x] Feature flag gating in config

Testing notes: Unit tests cover FSM transitions and ledger writes. Integration tests simulate a canary promote with injected regression in the post-shadow snapshot; the lock triggers and blocks promotion. E2E in benchmark-lab ran a 5000-sample dry-run to validate minimal impact on production queues when dry_run_traffic_fraction = 0.01. CI includes a synthetic replay of shadow traffic against the dry-run runner.

Operational safety: The hitl.lock has an operator-configurable timeout (default 12h) after which the rollout reverts to a 'timed_out' state that can either auto-abort or auto-approve depending on policy (conservative default: auto-abort). All approval actions are written to the audit log with actor, timestamp, and telemetry snapshot id. Audit entries integrate with the audit-log-exporter for downstream SIEM ingestion.

Backward compatibility & migration: The rollout spec change is additive and behind a feature flag. Existing rollouts without hitl.enabled behave as before. A small migration job (scripts/migrations/2026-02-add-hitl-field.sh) will annotate active rollouts with a default hitl object when enabling the feature for a tenant. Migration is non-blocking; operators are instructed to run it if they enable the feature in Private/Dedicated environments.

Why not fully automated? We observed two classes of regressions where automatic metrics gates produced false positives due to noisy upstream services and dataset skew; adding a low-friction human checkpoint allows an informed operator to combine automated telemetry with domain knowledge (e.g., release notes, dataset changes) before committing.

Related: Linear ENG-3821 (HITL rollout design), ENG-3899 (telemetry reconcile). References to earlier work: builds on the telemetry reconcile prototype from pr-60321-shadow-verifier-and-rollback-adapter.

Merge notes: squash-merge. Post-merge: enable feature flag in staging and run migration script, then schedule a brownout window with Platform to verify console UI for a handful of customers before wide enablement.
commits: 3 commits: 1) f3d4c2c - rollout: add HITL lock FSM and ledger persistence; 2) a9b7e1f - telemetry: add snapshot collector and reconcile diff; 3) 7c1d6b2 - console: add HITL operator view and approval actions + docs
review_comments: Marco Li requested: add an integration test where ledger is intentionally compacted during LOCKED state to validate restart behavior.
Renee Thompson requested: make hitl.timeout configurable per-tenant and clarify default in API docs.
Omar Velasquez comment: consider exposing the reconcile diff as a downloadable JSON blob for offline analysis; also ensure the size limit for snapshots prevents large payload blowups.
author_responses: Added test hitl_ledger_recovery in test/integration/hitl_e2e_test.go that simulates compaction and controller restart — addressed Marco's request.
Updated API docs and rollout migration script to accept per-tenant override of hitl.timeout; added example in docs/rollouts/hitl.md — addressed Renee's request.

Telemetry snapshots are capped to the compact format (metric aggregates + sample ids). Added downloadable JSON export and size-enforced truncation with a warning in the console — addressed Omar's comment.
post_merge_tasks: Enable feature flag in staging: infra/feature-flags/hitl=true
Schedule platform brownout window and run 3 guided HITL rollouts
incident_context: This PR was driven by a production regression on 2026-01-28 where an automated promote bypassed an intermittent downstream error spike. The investigation recommended short-circuiting automatic promotes with a lightweight human checkpoint for sensitive model upgrades.
notes: Feature is gated; recommend incremental enablement per-tenant. Contact on-call rollout-engineering for any blockers.
